title: First paid jobs and leaving home to join Ham Crawford
summary: He plays C-melody sax for $12.50, plays with small bands around Texas, runs off without permission, and joins Ham Crawford's band at sixteen.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Albert System clarinet is, of course, it's different from the band system clarinet, in that the band is an improved fingering mechanism. But, Albert is, I don't know, he just seemed to fall into it naturally. Easier to play by here, anybody who has, you'd say a little knack for it. But, I left home, actually, I became interested in playing, we had a little jazz band there in town. They had a band called Tim Shrill, not needed, but Tim Atkins. And, in this group, they had a Jewish drummer, Jake Goldberg, had a tenor saxophone player whose name was Carl Limburg, and Tim Atkins, an Englishman, was a pianist and leader. So, all the kids were excited about it. They were playing dances and making them, and they were a little bit older than our group. But, there was another little small group in town, and called the Melody Corps. And, they got a job that needed a saxophone player, and I didn't have a saxophone player. They said, you teach, you get a pair of long pants, then you get a C Melody Sax, we'll give you a job. So, I borrowed the sax, and they got me some long pants, and then we played Carthage, Texas, which is very close to Marshall's. And, we were $12.50 for our evening. And, that ended my delivering packages for the grocery store, drug store, and other places, because that seemed like an awful lot of money just to play three hours. So, from then on out, I continued to listen to other people who were better. And, before long, they started asking me to come up to Terrell, Texas, and Minniova, which are on the Dallas from Marshall. And, I had a pass on the Sunshine Special.

So, on Friday nights, I would go up and play with these little bands. Well, of course, I knew that I was going to play in a band. That's all I was going to say. I just had to do that. And, so, pretty soon, I just, without my father's permission, I just left and joined this little band. And, we went to Terrell, Texas, and played in a cafe. And, then we played nights in Athens and all the little Texas towns around 50 mile radius. And, this was really before I ever got out on the road to play with other territory of bands. But, we, I just, I often left. And, my father was very kind. And, instead of putting me on a reform school or something, my sister talked him out of being real bad to him. And, she said, well, I came back on, after this little incident. And, I guess I stayed maybe, went on to school, stayed for some months. And, then, Ham Crawford's band, which was said to be from Havana, Cuba. They'd been playing through East Texas, and they were extremely popular. And, Ham was really a very good saxophonist and had good musicians working there. So, he was one of the largest bands. So, they had three of us, a trio. So, he said, we're going to enlarge the band for six pieces and move another sax and playing that. So, I joined the band, again, without the permission of my folks. But, I just felt I had to do it, to me.
